name: AVAIO Digital Taurus
notes: Distinct from AVAIO's 'Leo' campus in Little Rock/Pulaski County AR — do not conflate. Site: East Metropolitan Center Business and Industrial Park, Brandon. Land acreage: AVAIO's own project page and groundbreaking materials cite 329 acres; the August 19 press release cited 175 acres — 329 used as more authoritative per operator's site. Capacity: 116 MW initial via executed ESA with Entergy Mississippi (energized June 2027 per operator site); Entergy guiding an additional 420 MW of grid power available by end of 2030; access to Gulf South Pipeline for up to 500 MW of on-site behind-the-meter thermal generation starting Q2 2027 — total baseload path to over 1 GW. The 116 MW planned figure reflects the executed first-phase ESA only; full buildout remains a projection. Investment: $6B stated without 'up to' qualifier across operator, MDA, and Governor's office sources; Governor's office describes it as the third-largest economic development project in Mississippi history. Jobs: 'at least 60 direct, high-tech jobs' and 'hundreds of indirect jobs ranging from construction to other related industries' — projections, not firm figures; no construction vs permanent breakdown confirmed. Rooftop solar of 20+ MW planned (behind-the-meter). Recycled water and new sewer line extension cited by operator as water infrastructure options. Estimated $23M in ad valorem tax revenue annually per Rankin First (county economic development group). Coordinates approximate (Brandon city center, Rankin County).

water.notes: Operator describes water-efficient cooling, rainwater recapture, cooling system economization (air-side economization implied), and recycled water as an available option. New sewer line extension under construction for wastewater. No specific MGD figure disclosed.

energy.notes: Initial 116 MW grid power via executed ESA with Entergy Mississippi (June 2027 target energization). Additional 420 MW grid power from Entergy projected by end of 2030. On-site thermal generation via Gulf South Pipeline access (up to 500 MW planned, Q2 2027 start) — on-site gas not yet built. Rooftop solar 20+ MW planned. Behind-the-meter generation noted by operator.

name: Amazon Boardman Exascale Data Center Campus
notes: Amazon confirmed the land purchase ($37M per Morrow County property records, confirmed by multiple news sources) but stated development plans are not final. Planning documents submitted to Morrow County describe a 1 GW exascale campus with 20 buildings across 4 million sq ft; Johnson Economics estimated $8B-$12B total investment. Land previously owned by Threemile Canyon Farms dairy. Distinct from Amazon's existing ~800 acres of operating/under-construction OR facilities. Lincoln Chronicle source URL returned 403 on fetch — primary claim supported by DCD source. energy.utility corrected from 'Bonneville Power Administration' (wholesale) to 'PacifiCorp (Pacific Power)' (retail utility). Coordinates are Boardman city centroid; exact site not publicly confirmed. Johnson Economics' economic-impact analysis (Morrow County Planning Commission, Jan 2025) models the full 1 GW campus at roughly $8 billion investment (potential range $7-12 billion), about 6,400 construction FTE over an eight-year build (~800/year) and about 560 operations FTE, assuming an Oregon Strategic Investment Program (SIP) property-tax abatement — modeled projections for a still-proposed campus, not firm commitments.

water.notes: Reflects Amazon's documented Oregon cooling practice — primarily free-air cooling with evaporative assist, with up to ~96% of cooling water returned to local farmers. Planning documents model roughly 35 million gallons/year for the full 1 GW campus (a projection). The specific cooling design for this proposed campus is not confirmed.

energy.notes: PacifiCorp (Pacific Power) is the local retail utility in Morrow County; AWS filed power complaints against PacifiCorp in November 2025 regarding insufficient capacity. BPA Columbia River hydroelectric generation underlies the Oregon grid and is a major component of what PacifiCorp delivers. AWS claims 95% renewable sourcing in Oregon. AWS also holds wind PPA (Leaning Juniper IIA, 98.4 MW) in same county.

name: AWS Costas Property Campus (Ridgeland)
notes: RESOLVES last wave's hold with independent primary-tier evidence that Canton and Ridgeland are genuinely two distinct AWS campuses, not a single project under two names. Mississippi Free Press (2026-08-19), reporting Madison County's denial of AWS's tax-valuation appeal, states directly: 'The county has entered into two fee-in-lieu-of-taxes agreements with the tech giant for its data center campuses in Canton and Ridgeland' -- i.e., Madison County's own tax/incentive administration treats these as two separate FILOT agreements, not one. Magnolia Tribune (2024-07-24, re-fetched this run) gives the physical distinction: the Madison County Mega Site is '927 acres ... located off Highway 22 and Nissan Parkway in Canton,' while the Costas Property is 'an additional 786 acres in Ridgeland ... located along the southern tip of Madison County near Tougaloo College, on the corner of Highland Colony Parkway and West County Line Road' -- roughly 20 miles apart. Both sites are within Madison County (Ridgeland is not a separate county), so the live aggregate record's id/framing as 'Madison County' is not wrong on that count, but it does combine two separately-incentivized campuses. Coordinates are the OSM-tagged traffic-signal node at the actual Highland Colony Parkway / West County Line Road intersection (confirmed via Overpass API query against current OpenStreetMap way data, not an estimate), not a confirmed parcel boundary -- precision 'approximate'. Deliberately omitted: capacityMw, investmentUsd, and jobs, because every figure found for this project (the $10B investment, the combined MW target, job counts) is stated for the two-site project as a whole; no source fetched this run apportions any of these by site, and apportioning by acreage share would be a fabricated estimate, not a sourced fact. See the companion refresh finding on aws-project-atlas-madison-county-ms recommending it be re-scoped to the Canton site alone.

name: AWS Project Green Campus
notes: Codename 'Project Green'; application filed via NorthPoint Development, LLC. Two-phase build-out: Phase 1 = 8 data center buildings; Phase 2 = 13 additional buildings (21 total). Located on ~1,000 acres at northeast quadrant of I-70 and Highway 19 interchange near New Florence. Official AWS/Governor Kehoe announcement on June 15, 2026 cited a $10B investment commitment. Earlier county planning documents and initial filings referenced a maximum capital investment ceiling of up to $35B — that figure is a speculative ceiling, not a committed amount. AWS separately announced a 138MW renewable energy project in Missouri; not confirmed as dedicated to this campus. Community investments included in announcement: $3M for county 911/emergency dispatch upgrades, $3M for community programs, $1M for Montgomery County Fairgrounds, $150K community fund, $50K teacher grant. Preserve Montgomery County LLC filed suit in February 2026 alleging ten counts of Missouri Sunshine Law violations (closed-session negotiations, NDAs with Amazon); case pending as of mid-2026. First buildings targeted operational by 2027; full campus potentially complete ~2032. Coordinates are approximate (parcel centroid at I-70 / Hwy 19 NE quadrant). Jobs: KOMU reported ~400 permanent jobs; DCD's coverage of the same $10B announcement cited no specific permanent figure (only 'thousands of construction jobs') — permanent count left unstructured pending firm corroboration.

water.notes: Water sourced from Cambrian-Ordovician aquifer via wells drilled to ~1,500 ft depth (to avoid impacting local private wells at shallower depths). Initial phase projected at 2.9M gallons/year; full 17-building campus projected at ~50M gallons/year (~0.137 MGD equivalent). Regional aquifer capacity exceeds 23 trillion gallons; current regional utilization ~8%; this project adds ~0.03%. On-site stormwater management ponds and water treatment plant planned. Cooling methodology not publicly specified.

energy.notes: Powered by Ameren Missouri grid. AWS committed to working with Ameren to ensure project energy costs are not passed to other ratepayers. AWS announced a separate 138MW renewable energy project in Missouri (not confirmed as on-site or dedicated to this campus).

name: Project Blue
notes: Unincorporated Pima County, west of Houghton Rd, near Tucson. 500-700MW planned across 13M sq ft (a range, so omitted from capacityMw). Beale's own letter of 2025-09-17 adds a qualifier the county FAQ omits: the figure "include[s] full-time contractors and support personnel", and at least 75 of the roles will be directly employed by the end user. Beale has also stated it "is not asking for property tax incentives, often a necessary component of a data center project's cost competitiveness", and the utility agreement with Tucson Electric Power carries no financial incentives or discounts — unusual for a project of this size, and the reason subsidies are recorded as absent rather than merely unsearched.

Water volume remains publicly contested — Beale has cited roughly 40 acre-feet/year while the ADWR permit ceiling is 96.5 acre-feet/year. name: Project Red Clay
notes: SUBSIDY — CONFIRMED ABSENCE AS OF 24 JULY 2026: Yellowhammer News reports that no formal abatement request had been filed as of that date, and that the granting body would be the Lowndes County Commission. Under legislation signed by Gov. Kay Ivey in April 2026, an abatement approved before 1 January 2027 could run up to 30 years; after that date the maximum is 20 years. No dollar amount has been stated by any source, so no subsidies entry is recorded. NO NAMED TENANT: Cloverleaf is described by Yellowhammer as a Houston- and Seattle-based speculative developer assembling land for an unnamed future operator; aiClassification is therefore "likely", not confirmed. CONFLICTING FIGURES, recorded rather than reconciled: investment is "$1.5 billion" per WSFA and Route Fifty ("at least $1.5 billion in the development stage") but the developer's own site says "Over a $1 billion taxable investment in Lowndes County". Jobs: the developer's site says "Over 1,000 high-paying construction jobs" and "at least 50 full-time jobs" once operational; other coverage this run could not fetch cites 1,000-1,500 construction and over 200 permanent — the developer's own lower figures are recorded here. Footprint: "more than 800 acres in northeast Lowndes County" and "2.88 million square feet" (Yellowhammer). ZONING: reporting notes Cloverleaf could buy and develop here because Lowndes County has no planning or zoning authority. Coordinates are the OSM-confirmed U.S. 80 / AL 21 junction that WSFA names as the site vicinity — NOT a parcel boundary; the actual footprint is somewhere in northeast Lowndes County near that junction. Inside Climate News and WBHM coverage of this project returned HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and curl in this run and is therefore not cited.

water.notes: Developer's project site states the building "will only use as much water as an office building on a day-to-day basis" and uses "a closed-loop cooling system requiring a one-time fill" — an explicitly recirculating circuit, hence closed_loop. Separately, a Cloverleaf representative told WSFA: "The most amount of water that we've asked for for consumption is 100,000 gallons of water per day." That is a requested maximum, not metered use, so it is NOT recorded as reportedMgd. The Pintlala Water System is named as the supplier in secondary coverage this run could not fetch (Inside Climate News and WBHM both returned 403), so the supplier name is deliberately omitted.

WSFA reports the site sits "underneath a 500 kV electrical line" near the U.S. 80 / Alabama 21 intersection, and that the company was still finalizing power contracts as of 4 June 2026. Distinct from the tracked Vantage Phoenix (Goodyear), Stream PHXA (Goodyear) and Microsoft Goodyear campuses — different operator and different parcel. Coordinates are the cited Bullard Avenue / Yuma Road intersection from OpenStreetMap; the campus lies to the northwest, so the pin is approximate.

water.notes: Compass describes 'advanced hybrid cooling that uses no water during operations'. Under the project's tie-breaker — a recirculating cooling circuit is closed_loop even where heat is finally rejected to air — this is recorded as closed_loop, not 'air'; the operator's own word 'hybrid' refers to the equipment, not to seasonal wet/dry switching.

energy.notes: On-site 230 kV substation.

name: Crusoe Warrenton Campus
notes: Coordinates approximate. Site address: 22151 NW Service Road, Warrenton MO; north of NW Service Road, west of Hwy. W. Two 805,000 sq ft data center buildings + 40,000 sq ft administration building + 621,250 sq ft Ameren-owned switch yard + 603,200 sq ft Crusoe-owned electrical substation. Crusoe described as its 'fifth campus' in its national AI data center portfolio as of June 2026 per Crusoe newsroom. Meta signed agreement with Crusoe in June 2026 for approximately 1.6GW of AI computing capacity split across Childress TX and Warrenton MO campuses — per-site split not disclosed; confirms Warrenton as AI anchor customer site (sourceRef 3). Status: conditional use permit and site plan approved; land disturbance review and construction permits still outstanding before groundbreaking. Crusoe committed publicly to seek no real property tax or gross receipt tax abatements; would pursue state incentives only (sourceRef 2). Developer projected annual property taxes ~$80M/year (sourceRef 1), with ~$44M to local schools. Construction jobs projected ~2,000-2,500 over ~3-year build; permanent tech jobs projected ~100 (developer estimates, sourceRef 1 and 2 — not firm contractual commitments). Crusoe historically used on-site flared natural gas but divested those operations; Warrenton campus is grid-connected via Ameren Missouri — no on-site gas generation reported here. Distinct from the Google/Crusoe 'Goodnight' campus in Armstrong County TX.

water.notes: Closed-loop cooling system using food-grade polypropylene glycol continuously recycled within the system; no reported MGD figure disclosed. Company claims 40% less water usage compared to a conventional light industrial facility (sourceRef 2).

energy.notes: Ameren Missouri owns and will operate the on-site switch yard; Crusoe owns the on-site electrical substation. Ameren signed confidential large-load agreements totaling 2.2GW with multiple Missouri data centers in February 2026; individual customer details not disclosed (sourceRef 8). No on-site gas generation reported for this campus.

name: Project Matador
notes: 11GW is the long-term ceiling for the HyperGrid campus; near-term company targets include 1GW by end of 2026 and 2.3GW first-phase delivery — these are company goals, not firm commitments. Land acreage reported variously (5,769 acres per DCD July 2025 and 5,855 acres per other sources; later company materials cite 7,570 acres on 7,570 acres); using 5,769 as the earliest confirmed figure, sourced from the gas turbine acquisition announcement. Coordinates approximate (seed-provided; site in Carson County ~12 miles NE of Amarillo, adjacent to DOE Pantex Plant). Fermi America co-founded January 2025 by former Texas Governor and U.S. Energy Secretary Rick Perry, Toby Neugebauer (CEO, departed April 2026 after being fired 'without cause'), and Griffin Perry. IPO raised $682M on Nasdaq under ticker FRMI (October 2025), valuing company at ~$19B at opening; market cap collapsed to ~$3.4B by April 2026 after leadership exits and loss of anchor tenant ($150M LOI canceled December 2025). Company organized as a REIT; had zero revenue at IPO. Investment: equipment financing commitments exceed $600M ($500M MUFG turbine warehouse + $200M Keystone/Cape facility); projected total project cost $70–90B is a range/projection, not a firm figure — omitted from investmentUsd per data-rigor policy. Jobs: 50,000+ projected across campus lifetime — projection only, omitted from jobs field. Nuclear campus name in NRC COLA filings: 'President Donald J. Trump Advanced Energy and Intelligence Campus'; publicly marketed as Project Matador / HyperGrid.

water.notes: No confirmed water use figures published. Community opposition raised concerns about Ogallala Aquifer impacts from combined cooling demand of gas plants and data centers. Arid Texas Panhandle location heightens water supply risk.

energy.notes: Initial generation: on-site natural gas. Fermi acquired 600MW+ of gas turbines in two deals (July 2025): 478MW from Firebird LNG/Siemens Energy (six SGT800 turbines + heat recovery steam generators + one SST600 steam turbine) and 135MW from GE 6B Frame units acquired from a New Jersey facility. TCEQ issued preliminary approval for up to 6GW of combined-cycle gas (November 2025); air permit secured February 2026 after ~279 public comments. Long-term plan adds four Westinghouse AP1000 reactors (~4.4GW nuclear baseload; COLA filed June 17 2025, NRC accepted two of three parts for review September 2025, Part 3 deadline December 31 2026, first reactor targeted 2031, all four by 2038) plus solar and battery storage. Fermi is also evaluating SMRs (MOU with Doosan Enerbility). Entire campus is behind-the-meter — private grid, no public utility offtake.

name: Goodnight Campus
notes: Campus name: Goodnight, near the town of Claude, TX (known address: 10001 Lima Rd, Claude, TX 79019). Coordinates approximate (based on dispatch seed; county parcel area). Developed by Crusoe Energy via entity GN DC1, LLC (Delaware LLC, 255 Filmore St., Denver, CO 80206); Google is the hyperscale tenant/customer, confirmed publicly November 2025. Tax abatement agreement was signed with GN DC1, LLC in late 2024 without publicly naming the tenant. Google confirmed the Crusoe partnership but had not signed an offtake agreement for the on-site gas plant as of early 2026; negotiations on power amounts still ongoing per Google spokesperson. Planned IT capacity: Phase 1 described in tax abatement agreement as 'anticipated to consume up to 530 MW,' 4 buildings each with 4 x 25 MW data halls, on approximately 350 acres; Phase 2 (possible additional 3+ buildings) reported at up to ~500 MW additional; combined full build-out reported as 1 GW+ — all capacity figures are 'up to' ceilings from permit and abatement documents, not firm contracted amounts. Project was scaled back from an original 7-building plan (October 2025 local reporting); 4 buildings with construction permits from TDLR as of early 2026; Crusoe described 3-4 buildings as likely; grading on additional parcels suggests total program may reach 5+ buildings. First phase expected online 2026; initial county PILOT payment expected June/July 2026. The $40B Google Texas investment is a statewide commitment through 2027 covering multiple sites (Armstrong County, Haskell County, Ellis County) with no site-specific investment figure disclosed by Google. A $29B campus investment figure appeared in Aterio/Crusoe reporting — this is a projected ceiling, not a firm committed amount; omitted from investmentUsd per data-rigor policy. Distinct from Google's separate Haskell County TX site and Red Oak (Ellis County) TX sites — do not conflate. Building 3 is scheduled for completion 2026-08-01; Building 4 is due March 2027. Nothing at the campus is yet described as operational.

water.notes: No water volume or cooling system type disclosed in sources reviewed. TCEQ wastewater permit WQ0016881001 filed under the same GN DC1 LLC entity, indicating water infrastructure is being permitted; no public details available on cooling approach or projected water consumption.

energy.notes: Crusoe Energy filed TCEQ air construction permit (TCEQ announcement Feb 5, 2026) for a 933 MW natural gas power plant on-site at the Goodnight campus. Gas plant operates off-grid with no ERCOT grid connection for this generation asset. No carbon capture technology. Estimated emissions up to 4.5 million tons CO2/year and 1,600 tons criteria air pollutants/year per permit application. A portion of the campus also co-locates behind the meter with Goodnight Wind farm (265.5 MW, Serena Energy, came online 2024) under Texas SB6 net metering arrangement; proposal submitted to Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT), regulatory review ongoing as of mid-2026. Separate TCEQ wastewater permit WQ0016881001 filed under same entity, indicating water/utility infrastructure planning underway.

The address '902 East Leith Street, Flint, MI' for the broader former Buick City complex is independently confirmed by two fetched sources: Genesee County View's 2023-05-25 piece on Ashley Capital's adjacent 'Flint Commerce Center' redevelopment ('The site address provided in the article is: 902 E. Leith St. in Flint'), and EPA's own 2023-11-01 press release on the Flint Commerce Center LLC prospective-purchaser agreement for 'roughly 330 acres of the former Buick City manufacturing facility.' Leith Street is independently documented (via a non-cited Wikipedia cross-check, used only to sanity-check geography, not as a source) as the street that divides the ~413-acre Buick City site into northern and southern sections, and the chosen Leith Street road segment (of several OpenStreetMap-tagged segments) falls within the site's other documented boundary streets (E Pierson Rd to the north, N Saginaw St/Industrial to the west, E Hamilton Ave to the south, James P Cole Blvd to the east -- all geocoded this run to confirm the bounding box). This is the general Buick City site address, NOT a confirmed parcel boundary for Hillwood-Sterling's specific ~200-acre sub-parcel within it (Ashley Capital, not Hillwood-Sterling, is RACER Trust's direct purchaser of the larger site; Hillwood-Sterling's deal, per Gander Newsroom, is reported as a ~200-acre interest within the broader former Buick City footprint) -- precision 'approximate' reflects both the geocode-not-parcel caveat AND this sub-parcel uncertainty. name: IREN Sweetwater Campus
notes: Two-site campus: Sweetwater 1 (1,400 MW, ~1,700 acres, Nolan/Jones County boundary area) substation energized May 1, 2026 via 345kV ERCOT connection; data centers commissioning in phases. Sweetwater 2 (600 MW, ~500 acres, Fisher County, near Hamlin TX, ~28 miles from SW1) targeted energization late 2027 per IREN (some sources cite 2028). Direct fiber loop planned between sites for single 2 GW compute hub with <10ms latency to Dallas. Coordinates are approximate (Sweetwater city center, Nolan County seat). County boundary sources conflicting: DCD says Fisher County for both sites; interconnection.fyi and dispatch brief cite Nolan County for SW1; northwiseproject.com says Nolan and Jones Counties span the campus. IREN's $9.7B Microsoft contract (Nov 2025) and $3.4B NVIDIA contract (May 2026) are company-wide deals currently deployed at Childress, TX campus (Horizon 1-4); the NVIDIA partnership press release specifically names Sweetwater as the flagship future deployment site for NVIDIA DSX factory architecture. No confirmed customer contracts specific to Sweetwater site as of 2026-07-07. IREN was in Sweetwater since 2022 as a Bitcoin mining site; HPC/AI pivot announced October 2024. Interconnection.fyi lists renewable energy sourcing via RECs (wind/solar) at this site.

water.notes: Direct-to-chip liquid cooling plus supplemental air cooling. West Texas arid climate noted as a water-conservation design driver. No reported MGD figure confirmed.

energy.notes: 345kV high-voltage connection to ERCOT grid. IREN and third-party sources describe West Texas as one of the world's largest renewable energy markets; interconnection.fyi lists renewable energy via RECs (wind/solar) for this site.

The testimony states Evest 'seeks to develop adjacent to Laidley's data center in Richland Parish, Louisiana, that was the subject of the proceedings in LPSC Docket No. U-37425' (i.e., the already-tracked Hyperion project). To serve Evest, Entergy is seeking certification of seven new 754 MW 1x1 CCCT generators (four near the Richland Parish site, three sited near the existing Big Cajun site in Pointe Coupee Parish) plus battery storage co-located at the Bogalusa West Solar and Cypress Harvest Solar facilities -- on top of the three CCCTs (Franklin Farms 1&2, Waterford 5) already approved for Hyperion itself. Investigative coverage (The Lens, 2026-04-14) puts the combined Hyperion+Evest generation build at 10 new gas plants, 7,000+ MW, and $16B+ in new fossil-fuel infrastructure serving this one customer, and reports the underlying Entergy-Meta commercial agreements are not fully public. name: Microsoft Fairwater Atlanta (Azure AI Superfactory)
notes: 615-acre, up-to-13-building QTS-built campus on Hwy 54W near Fayetteville, Fayette County (Microsoft's materials say 'Atlanta'). Began operation Oct 2025 as Fairwater 2 — a 'multi-gigawatt' AI campus. ~1,500 MW is the anticipated ultimate Georgia Power load across all buildings (planned figure; ~433 MW cited as initially online). Distinct from Microsoft's smaller Tyrone, GA campus. Two-story design with no UPS or backup generators. Coordinates are the Fayetteville area centroid. Microsoft has not disclosed tenant capex for the Fairwater Fayetteville space; the ~$1B/$6.5B figures are QTS developer build-out estimates for the full multi-tenant campus, and the widely-cited $14.5M abatement / $1.8B / $75M figures attach to different Microsoft/Fulton-County sites (the $75M was FCDA land-sale proceeds, not a subsidy to QTS) -> investmentUsd omitted.

water.notes: QTS closed-loop 'water-free' design (COO Ryan Hunter: 'Once the water's in there, it stays in there for the life of the asset'); ~600,000-gal one-time fill per building, ongoing per-building use 'equivalent to four American households per month.' During construction the campus drew ~29-30M gallons through two unmetered connections (2024-25); Fayette County issued a ~$147,000 retroactive charge and no fine. No operational daily figure for the Microsoft tenant space specifically.

energy.notes: Two-story design with no UPS or backup generators (DCD, Oct 2025) — no on-site generation. Microsoft states Fairwater uses improved closed-loop cooling that 'consumes almost zero water in its operation.' Georgia Power 2025 IRP testimony cites the QTS Fayetteville campus as a single load of just under 1,500 MW at full build-out.

City department figures show 1.1 million gallons/year municipal water draw (Inquirer, Jan 2026); a separate source (WHYY) cites 'up to 20 million gallons annually' — discrepancy unresolved, likely reflecting different accounting (total throughput vs. net municipal draw). name: PORTS-Pike Technology Campus
notes: Officially "PORTS-Pike Technology Campus"; formerly tracked under the pre-announcement Ohio entity New Day Data Centers LLC, a name that appears nowhere in the SEC S-1 or SB Energy’s own announcements. Developer/operator is SB Energy (SoftBank-controlled); the DOE lease was signed 2026-02-26 by its subsidiary Pike County Portsmouth DC LLC. CAPACITY - three distinct figures that must not be conflated: 8.0 GW-IT of contracted compute (8,024 MW-IT; NVIDIA guarantees the initial 4.25 GW-IT with an option on the remaining 3.78 GW-IT), 10 GW of gross power load (the capacityMw.planned value here), and 9.2 GW of new gas generation. OFFTAKE: on 2026-08-17 SB Energy subsidiaries signed 17 twenty-year triple-net leases with OpenAI, with rent commencement conditioned on interconnection and generation being available; NVIDIA provided a residual-value guaranty capped at $105B and separately bought $1.5B of non-voting stock. LAND: landAcres is intentionally omitted - the DOE lease covers 189 acres (Batch 1) on which "one data center building is expected to be constructed", while the S-1 places the buildings "across several thousand acres of private property"; the widely-cited 3,700/3,777 acres is the whole federal reservation, which also hosts the separately tracked Oklo Aurora project, Centrus and the DUF6 plant. INVESTMENT: investmentUsd intentionally omitted - $10B (DOE, March) and $30-40B (project site) describe the same ~800 MW first phase and cannot both be right, the $67.2B total appears only as one trade outlet’s unattributed rollup, and the S-1 states no total capex. SUBSIDIES: none awarded - the Ohio Tax Credit Authority minutes record no award, no JobsOhio award was found, and Ohio paused new data-centre tax exemptions in May 2026; a county PILOT is under negotiation because the leased federal land yields no property tax. STATUS: early civil works began after the 2026-03-20 groundbreaking, though the S-1 lists construction as not started, with first capacity in 2028 and full buildout 2032. Distinct from oklo-aurora-pike-county-oh on the same broader site - do not merge or double-count.

energy.notes: S-1: the campus is "designed to include 8.0 GW-IT of data center capacity, representing 10 GW of gross power load expected to be supported by the PJM transmission system and new neighbouring gas-fired generation facilities" - hence "mixed". The 9.2 GW of gas is new build, not a reused plant; the site is the former Portsmouth uranium-enrichment complex, whose historic power came over OVEC coal-fired transmission (X-533 switchyard, de-energised 2008, decommissioned 2011). Recorded under onSiteGenerationMw as dedicated captive generation, but note the S-1 calls the plants "neighbouring": they sit ~5 miles south of Piketon adjacent to the DOE site, are developed by "an affiliate of SoftBank that is not our subsidiary", and SB Energy "do[es] not expect to own or operate" them. Ohio Power Siting Board case 26-0746-EL-BGN (applicant Portsmouth Gas DevCo, LLC) covers only a first tranche of "up to 2 gigawatts"; AEP Ohio transmission (new 765 kV Baku-Gavin line and four substations) is a separate docket. AEP grid capex is stated as $4.2B by DOE and ~$5.1B in the S-1, unreconciled. CAUTION: the project site states the gas generation "will be owned by the U.S. Government", but the S-1 says "no binding agreement has been executed between us or any of our affiliates and any governmental entity with respect to the funding, construction, ownership or operation of the generation facilities" - do not assert federal ownership. Only ~0.8 GW of gross load has contracted utility service so far.

name: Poolside Project Horizon AI Campus
notes: 2 GW AI training campus on a 568-acre parcel of the Mitchell family's Longfellow Ranch in Pecos County, near Fort Stockton. Coordinate anchored on Fort Stockton (nearest named town in coverage); exact parcel not publicly disclosed. CoreWeave was original anchor tenant (15-year, 250 MW lease, 40,000 Nvidia GB300 GPUs) but terminated the lease in late March 2026 after Poolside's Series C funding round failed to close; site reported idle as of mid-2026. Not a community finding, but material and worth flagging for maintainer review: CoreWeave (the announced anchor tenant) mutually terminated its agreement for Project Horizon around April 2026 after Poolside failed to stand up its first GPU cluster on schedule, and Poolside's associated ~$2B Nvidia-led funding round also fell through. As of late July 2026 Poolside was seeking a replacement partner (reportedly including Google) for up to 400MW, with no anchor tenant signed as of that reporting. The record's status ('proposed') isn't necessarily wrong, but the originally announced 2GW/CoreWeave deal that justified the record no longer stands as described. The dispatching brief for this run scoped only 'community' fields -- flagging this rather than silently omitting it, since fields.community does not fit this fact.

energy.notes: Designed in eight 250-MW phases powered primarily by on-site aeroderivative gas turbines fueled by Permian Basin natural gas; site adjacent to a major gas-processing hub.

name: Prado AI / PraCon Global AI Industrial Campus
notes: Net-new but SPECULATIVE — confidence 'rumored' on purpose. A proposed AI/semiconductor industrial campus with its own private power plant, before the Mississippi PSC. Deliberately omitted, because the developer refused to state them: capacity MW, investment, acreage, site parcel, timeline. Prado told Mississippi Today he declined to give the PSC more detail because 'making that information available to the utility companies would take away the project's competitive advantage,' and Prado AI 'is still working on securing all the funding it would need for a project of this size'; the only figure attached to it is Prado's stated LONG-TERM GOAL of 'over $25 billion', which is an aspiration, not an announced investment, and is therefore NOT recorded in investmentUsd. Location: the March PSC filing named Ridgeland, but Prado has since said only 'the Jackson metro area' and declined to say where — coordinates are a Ridgeland city geocode from the filing, precision 'approximate'; if it lands elsewhere in the metro this record needs relocating. Sourced from a Wayback snapshot because mississippitoday.org returns HTTP 403 to direct fetches. Ed's call whether a project this unformed belongs in the dataset at all; the argument for including it is that it is docketed at the PSC and formally opposed by both of the state's major utilities, which is more than a press rumour. NOTE the separate real facility entergy-traceview-ridgeland-ms is also in Ridgeland — unrelated.

sources.label: Mississippi developer plans to move forward with data center plans, even as state declines to give ruling (Wayback snapshot 2026-08-19)

community.notes: Not a residents-vs-site dispute: the documented opposition is regulatory and commercial. Entergy Mississippi and Mississippi Power, the state's two largest power providers, are protesting the effort, arguing the arrangement would make Prado AI a public utility subject to PSC regulation, and that a certificate of public convenience and necessity would be required to build the generator. Mississippi Power's brief warned the request 'could intentionally or unintentionally upset this delicate regulatory balance.' No public-reception evidence from nearby residents appears in the source.

statusHistory.note: Prado AI, an affiliate of PraCon Global Investment, asked the Mississippi Public Service Commission for an opinion on whether it would be regulated as a public utility if it generated and supplied power to tenants at a potential data center and semiconductor manufacturing campus; its initial filing said the campus would be in Ridgeland and that electricity would be included in the lease and not metered.

The PSC declined to issue an opinion, calling the request 'premature' and 'hypothetical' and saying it lacked enough information; Commissioner De'Keither Stamps said Prado did not answer basic questions such as how many tenants the power would serve. Prado said the company will proceed anyway.

name: Project River Data Center
notes: THE DATA-CENTER TENANT IS NOT CONFIRMED. Wright Brothers Construction CEO Mitchell Simpson told Mix 104.1 WCLE on 2026-08-26 that the power plant is certain but its offtaker is not: "We definitely know we're developing a power plant... We don't know what it's going to power yet... It potentially could be a data center, but it very well could be something else," naming advanced manufacturing, robotics and semiconductor manufacturing as alternatives, before adding that with that much power "it's very likely going to be that." The company's own 2026-08-26 release describes the campus as "anchored by an on-site power plant and data center." Recorded at confidence 'reported' for that reason. Roughly 850 acres of privately-owned Wright family land west of I-75 and north of Old Lower River Road NW, along the Hiwassee River in northern Bradley County near I-75 Exit 33, submitted for rezoning and annexation into the City of Cleveland on 2026-08-25. The $11.3bn headline is the whole campus; $7.3bn is the data-center portion as itemised in press coverage. Groundbreaking is not expected until end of 2027 and the build is phased over 60 months. Coordinates are a geocode of Lower River Road NW, not the parcel; no source states lat/lon. No state or local incentive agreement is named in any of the three sources.

water.notes: The developer states the campus makes its own water by recovering moisture as biomass dries, running on a closed loop, and says it recovers enough clean water annually to supply both the power plant and the anchor tenant with no day-to-day draw on the municipal system. CEO Mitchell Simpson told Mix 104.1 WCLE the biomass process yields 200 gallons per minute of usable internal water for cooling loops and that the plant needs no river intake or discharge pipes. Classified closed_loop on the recirculating-circuit rule; the sources do not state the heat-rejection equipment.

energy.notes: Powered behind the meter by the co-located Project River energy campus (500 MW biomass plus 1,000 MW natural gas), with a requested 360 MW TVA interconnection for backup and peaking only. Developers say no diesel generators.

name: QTS Bessemer (Project Marvel)
notes: Codename: Project Marvel. 18-building hyperscale campus on Red Ridge near I-459 and I-20/59 interchange in Bessemer (Jefferson County). Announced capacity: up to 1,200 MW at full build-out — reported as a planned ceiling, roughly 9% of Alabama Power's current generating capacity; recorded as capacityMw.planned = 1200 (an announced 'up to' full-build-out ceiling, consistent with how the dataset records other announced full-build-out figures). Investment: reported at $14–14.5B across sources (Logistics Land Investment anticipated 'close to $14.4B'; WBRC reported $14.5B at November 2025 rezoning; DCD reported ~$14B); no single firm company-confirmed figure exists — treated as a projected cost range and excluded from investmentUsd. Land: ~1,607.42 acres total after two rezoning rounds (initial ~700 acres November 2025 + 914-acre expansion April 2026). QTS affiliate purchased land from TPA Group affiliate for $431.73M. Chapter 9B statutory eligibility would have provided a 30-year abatement estimated at $500M+; QTS committed not to seek local property tax incentives (per WBRC July 2026) — subsidy excluded as eligibility does not equal award and QTS renounced pursuit. Full buildout timeline: 7+ years. Birmingham Business Alliance estimated ~$4B net benefit over 30 years; Bessemer City Schools projected ~$25M/year. AI framing not officially confirmed by QTS or the city as of July 2026 — size and scale (hyperscale, cloud/AI demand framing in QTS statement) support 'likely' classification. Coordinates are approximate for the Red Ridge parcel area. Jobs: ~1,000 construction and ~330 permanent are projected figures for the proposed (not-yet-built) campus (WBRC, Nov 2025) — recorded as projections in notes, not structured jobs fields, per data-rigor policy. QTS Data Centers is owned by Blackstone (2021 take-private). STATUS JUDGEMENT SURFACED, NOT APPLIED: Bessemer approved land-use rezonings for this campus in November 2025 and again (914 acres) in April 2026, which under the wave's rule that a rezoning approval means permitted could argue for permitted rather than proposed. I did not change it, because the record's own cited source dated 2026-07-02 postdates both rezonings and still describes the campus as proposed, and no building permit or site-preparation start was found in any source fetched this run. A maintainer should decide whether a rezoning alone promotes this record.

name: Riverview Innovation & Technology Campus
notes: Site: former Tonawanda Coke Corporation coke-manufacturing plant (operated 1917-2018; TCC bankruptcy), 3875 & 3800 River Road, Town of Tonawanda, Erie County NY - 140 acres. Brownfield developer Jon M. Williams completed acquisition Oct. 10, 2019 and has led an estimated $100M remediation; Honeywell (successor to Allied Chemical/TCC predecessor) also involved. 500,000 sq ft facility proposed. Coordinates are approximate for the River Road parcel. Note: one source names 'Niagara County' but Buffalo News, BTPM, and WBEN independently and consistently identify this as the Town of Tonawanda, Erie County (distinct from the separate City of North Tonawanda in Niagara County) - Erie County used here per majority/independent-source cross-check. NO STATUS CHANGE. As of June 2026 the SEQRA/site-plan review was paused pending NYISO and National Grid results; no permit or construction approval exists. Remains proposed. CONFIRMED ABSENCE (re-checked 2026-09-10, reporting dated 2026-07): the Riverview project had not requested any IDA subsidy as of this reporting, and Erie County's executive has said he would not support the county IDA granting it tax breaks.

water.notes: Community opposition specifically cited cooling-system noise (24/7 operation, cited by residents as 75-105+ decibels) as a top concern at the June 3, 2026 Planning Board meeting; specific cooling technology not yet disclosed by the developer.

energy.notes: Developer states ~91% emission-free electricity due to proximity to the Niagara Power Project (hydro) and Nine Mile Point Nuclear Station. SEQRA/site plan review temporarily paused while awaiting NYISO and National Grid clarification on transmission-upgrade costs/timeline. A $50M on-site electrical substation is planned.

name: STREAM U.S. Data Centers at STAMP
notes: Proposed three-building hyperscale campus at the Western New York Science, Technology and Advanced Manufacturing Park (STAMP), Town of Alabama, Genesee County - by capital investment the largest data center proposal found for New York in this run. GCEDC states a "$19.46 billion" capital investment and "$285 million in PILOT/host revenues" for Genesee County, the Town of Alabama and the Oakfield-Alabama Central School District, with a public hearing "Thursday, March 19 at 7 p.m. at the Town of Alabama Fire Hall, 2230 Judge Road, Basom, NY 14013." Investigative Post reports the incentive package as "$1.46 billion in tax breaks for the creation of 125 jobs," of which "$1.43 billion in sales tax breaks" and "a $31 million mortgage tax break"; those two components are recorded as separate subsidy entries rather than the rounded total. capacityMw.planned = 500 records the sentence "Stream has said it will use 500 megawatts of electricity, more than 80 percent of all the power available at the STAMP industrial park" - this is stated electricity USE, not a certified IT load or an interconnection award. CONFLICTING FIGURES, recorded honestly: (a) acreage - Investigative Post says the campus spans "over 90 acres at the 1,250-acre industrial park" and landAcres is set to 90; an aggregator listing gives 130 acres and was NOT verified, so it is not used. (b) construction jobs - GCEDC's CEO is quoted at "an additional 1,000 workers temporarily," while "the agency reports on its cost-benefit analysis for the project which says construction will employ more than 16,000"; the lower, attributed figure is recorded. (c) capital cost has moved from "$6.3 billion a year ago" to "$11 billion" to "$19 billion"; the GCEDC-published $19.46B is used. Confirmed absences (2026-09-09): no source fetched states a water withdrawal volume for the campus, a confirmed hydropower allocation (the Tonawanda Seneca Nation letter opposes a prospective allocation, which is not the same as one being granted), or a construction start date - so no energy field is recorded. aiClassification is 'likely': the project is universally described as an AI-boom data campus but no fetched source states the workload. Coordinates are geocoded to the Town of Alabama, Genesee County, NOT to a confirmed parcel. This is a REQUESTED figure, not a confirmed/awarded PILOT -- at the time of this reporting (2026-07) Gov. Hochul was considering a moratorium measure that could block it entirely. Flag for hand review: record explicitly as 'requested', not granted. SUBSIDY NOT RECORDED AS A FIELD (maintainer adjudication 2026-09-10): reporting describes a REQUESTED package worth about $1.46bn from the Genesee County IDA for the STAMP site, not an awarded one — at the time of the 2026-07 reporting the Governor was weighing a moratorium measure that could block it entirely. The `subsidies` schema has no granted-versus-requested distinction, so publishing the figure there would present unawarded money as awarded. Recorded here instead; promote it to a `subsidies` entry only once an executed IDA agreement is in hand.

name: Switch Pyramid Campus

I did NOT propose 'operational' because the only opening evidence I could fetch predates the record's own 2025-01 basis, so the maintainer may have chosen 'under_construction' deliberately to track the ongoing second/third-building expansion. name: Buckeye Tech Corridor
notes: Master-planned data center park on a ~2,069-acre former residential (Cipriani) parcel Tract acquired for ~$136M, south of I-10 in Buckeye; planned for up to ~20M sq ft across as many as 40 data centers at full build-out over ~15 years (~$20B). Coordinates are an approximate town-level geocode (Buckeye, south of I-10), not a parcel-confirmed point. The City of Buckeye executed a development agreement with AZLCO Buckeye, LLC (Ordinance No. 08-24, adopted unanimously 2024-08-06). It reimburses the developer for six enumerated regional infrastructure components it builds and dedicates to the city — two public-safety sites, temporary and permanent public-safety facilities, $15M toward the Johnson Road interchange, and oversized regional water infrastructure — funded by 20% of the tax revenue the project itself generates, beginning only after the city has received $60M cumulatively and terminating 20 years from the effective date. It is capped at "the lesser of" the developer's verified costs or $50,000,000, so it cannot exceed what the developer actually spent; it is cost recovery for public infrastructure rather than an incentive, abatement or credit, and is therefore not recorded as a subsidy. Nothing has been paid to date. Buckeye's economic-development director has projected "more than 360 jobs at full build out" — an end-state across as many as 40 separate future data centers, none yet leased, permitted or built, and so not recorded as a permanent-jobs figure for this site. A search of 226 Buckeye Council and P&Z agendas (Feb 2024 – Aug 2026) found no GPLET and no Foreign Trade Zone instrument.

energy.notes: Buckeye Tech Corridor is planned around a standard APS grid interconnect; APS is working to expand area power infrastructure to serve up to 1.8GW of demand.

name: La Osa Data Center Park
notes: Vermaland LLC is a Phoenix-area land developer and land-banking company (CEO Kuldip 'Ken' Verma, founded 2006, controls ~25,000 acres of metro Phoenix land). DCD explicitly noted 'it is unclear whether Vermaland would operate its own data center facilities' — Vermaland plans to sell or rent parcels/buildings to tenants. No end tenants or hyperscaler operators have been named as of July 2026. Original plan: 59 data centers, up to 3 GW capacity ceiling, up to $33B investment ceiling, 3,300-acre site south of Eloy along the Greene Canal. A separate adjacent 1,700-acre parcel already holds Industrial-2 zoning for data centers, gas plants, battery storage, and solar. After strong public opposition (all ~60 public comments opposed), operator announced May 2026 scale-back to 11 data centers and 1 GW ceiling. Board of Supervisors hearing scheduled August 26, 2026; no permits issued as of record date. Site lies adjacent to a Qualified Opportunity Zone (investor tax benefit; not a direct subsidy to Vermaland — no subsidy award confirmed, omitted). Coordinates are approximate (parcel south of Eloy city center along Greene Canal; no precise APN published). $33B investment and all GW figures are announced ceilings, not firm commitments.

water.notes: Developer's attorney stated commitment to air-cooled or closed-loop cooling to minimize water demand. Site borders the Greene Canal, raising concerns about water access and consumption in an arid region. No MGD figures have been published. Critics cited Pima County's 'Project Blue' hyperscale data center as a cautionary precedent for water misuse in Arizona desert developments.

energy.notes: Phase 1 would rely on on-site natural gas turbines as primary power source, transitioning to solar as adjacent solar projects come online. Utility-scale battery storage included in original 3 GW plan. Hybrid model: gas + solar + battery + WAPA grid. On-site generation MW not specified in any source.

Pinal County Planning & Zoning Commission holds non-voting informational session July 17, 2025.

April 17, 2026: Pinal County land-use committee recommends advancing to full rezoning and site-plan review. No construction authorization granted; comprehensive plan amendment, drainage, flood mitigation, and road improvements still required.

May 2026: Operator announces 80% scale-back after all ~60 public comments opposed the project — revised plan reduces to 11 data centers and a 1 GW energy demand ceiling (down from 59 DCs / 3 GW). Board of Supervisors hearing rescheduled to August 26, 2026.

The Pinal County Board of Supervisors voted 4-1 on August 26, 2026 to reject the La Osa Energy Center rezoning request and development plans, after the developer had already scaled the proposal back roughly 80% (from 59 data center buildings and 3 GW of demand to 11 buildings, a 500 MW gas plant, battery storage and a 1 GW cap) in response to opposition over aquifer drawdown and incomplete energy sourcing plans. Supervisor Stephen Miller cast the lone dissent. Recorded as cancelled because the entitlement the project required was denied; Vermaland has not publicly announced a withdrawal or a refiling, so this reflects the county's denial rather than a developer decision.

notes: US Development sought a pre-application meeting with Osceola County planning (held Oct. 15, 2024) to discuss rezoning 434 acres in rural Yeehaw Junction from agricultural to industrial for nine three-story data center buildings (675,000 sq ft each, >7M sq ft total), a 15-acre on-site substation, and on-site water/wastewater treatment, with FPL as the named electrical provider. name: Tooele Valley Data Center Campus
notes: 500MW on-site gas-fired data center campus (~200-600 acre portion of a larger ~600-acre Tooele Valley Public Infrastructure District development that also includes a truck stop, hotel, and warehouses near I-80); backed by Utah Inland Port Authority financing. Developer plans a reverse-osmosis plant discharging ~250,000 gallons/day of brine into Great Salt Lake wetlands, drawing significant local opposition. Subsidies checked (2026-09-08): no site-level subsidy confirmed for this parcel. A $4.875M Utah Inland Port Authority Infrastructure Bank loan was reported in April 2024 to Zenith Bolinder, LLC — the Delaware LLC that petitioned UIPA in March 2024 to create the Tooele Valley Public Infrastructure District, representing 100% of surface property owners within it, and which KSL describes as "a partnership with longtime Utah developer Zenith Development"; Charles Akerlow appears both as the petition's contact sponsor and as Zenith Development's managing director. The two are affiliated but are not the same legal entity, the loan terms were not confirmed against a primary document, and the district's boundary exhibit is a scanned image that could not be read — so whether that loan reaches this data-centre parcel is unresolved. UIPA's executive director stated in July 2026 that the authority's involvement covers transportation within a 600-acre portion and does not extend to the southern section planned for the data centre.
